Top dressing a lawn with sand is a leveling technique used to correct uneven surfaces, fill low spots, and improve drainage in soil that compacts easily or retains too much moisture. The process works best when the lawn is first mowed as short as possible and aerated to break up the existing soil, which allows the sand to work down into the surface rather than sitting on top of the grass. A thin layer of screened topsoil is often applied before the sand to introduce nutrients that sand alone cannot provide, since sand has no organic matter and does not retain fertilizer or moisture on its own. Overseeding at the same time takes advantage of the fresh soil contact created by the top dressing, allowing new grass seed to germinate directly against the soil surface for faster and denser growth. #lawn #diy #garden #homeowner #outdoors

✨ Want a stunning, weed-free flower bed? Try this easy "pot-in-pot" landscaping hack to keep your borders looking fresh all year long! 📦 First, lay down cardboard along your path and space out heavy-duty black base pots on top. The cardboard acts as an amazing, natural weed barrier. 💧 Next, pour gravel all around the base pots. This hides the cardboard, holds your base pots securely in place, and provides excellent water drainage. 🪴 Now just drop your decorative plants-still in their own nursery pots-directly into the base pots! You can swap them out in seconds when seasons change or easily lift them inside if a freeze hits. 💡 Pro-tips: Mix up your flower colors, put the taller plants in the back, and always match your plants to the amount of sunlight that wall gets.
